findings.title: Public web app to subscription Owner via managed identity and Key Vault
findings.description: An internet-facing App Service has a system-assigned managed identity that can read a Key Vault holding a service principal credential. That principal holds roleAssignments/write at the subscription scope, enabling self-elevation to Owner.
findings.attack_vector: Public web entry -> SSRF/code exec -> managed identity token -> Key Vault secret -> privileged SP -> roleAssignments/write -> subscription Owner
findings.risk: Full administrative control of the production subscription, including all data stores and the ability to disable logging.
findings.recommendation: Remove roleAssignments/write from the service principal (replace with PIM-eligible, time-bound assignment). Scope the managed identity's Key Vault access to only the secrets it needs and enable Key Vault RBAC with purge protection.

evidence.summary: App Service contoso-public-portal exposes HTTPS publicly with system-assigned identity enabled.
SP 'sp-deploy-prod' holds a custom role with Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write at subscription scope.
Key Vault kv-web-prod grants get/list secrets to the app's managed identity via access policy.

findings.title: Storage account allows anonymous public blob access
findings.description: Storage account 'contosopublicdata' has allowBlobPublicAccess enabled and a container with an anonymous access level of 'container', allowing unauthenticated enumeration and download of all blobs.
findings.attack_vector: Unauthenticated internet user lists and downloads blobs directly over HTTPS.
findings.risk: Exposure of any sensitive data stored in the public container; reconnaissance aid for further attacks.
findings.recommendation: Set allowBlobPublicAccess=false on the storage account and set every container's public access level to 'private'. Use SAS or Entra-authenticated access for legitimate sharing.

defender_for_cloud: Storage account public access should be disallowed

findings.title: Service principal holds roleAssignments/write at subscription scope
findings.description: The CI/CD service principal 'sp-deploy-prod' is assigned a custom role that includes Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write — an escalation primitive that lets the principal grant itself Owner.
findings.attack_vector: Any compromise of the SP credential yields a one-step path to subscription Owner.
findings.risk: Privilege escalation to full subscription control; this is the pivot that turns the public-web entry point into a Critical chain.
findings.recommendation: Replace the standing assignment with a least-privilege deployment role that excludes roleAssignments/write. If role assignment is required, gate it behind PIM with approval.

findings.title: Network security group allows RDP (3389) from the internet
findings.description: NSG 'nsg-jumpbox' has an inbound rule allowing TCP 3389 from source 0.0.0.0/0 (Any). The associated VM is directly reachable for RDP brute-force.
findings.attack_vector: Internet-wide RDP brute force / credential stuffing against the jumpbox.
findings.risk: Initial access foothold on a management host with line of sight to internal resources.
findings.recommendation: Remove the 0.0.0.0/0 RDP rule. Use Azure Bastion or just-in-time VM access, and restrict management ports to known admin IP ranges.

evidence.summary: Rule 'allow-rdp' — protocol TCP, destPort 3389, source Any, access Allow.

defender_for_cloud: Management ports should be closed on your virtual machines

findings.title: Privileged accounts without multi-factor authentication
findings.description: Three accounts holding the Global Administrator role have no registered MFA method and are not covered by a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA.
findings.attack_vector: Password-only access to tenant-wide admin; phishing or credential stuffing yields Global Admin.
findings.risk: Compromise of any one account grants full control of the Entra tenant and all subscriptions.
findings.recommendation: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all privileged roles via Conditional Access, and make the roles PIM-eligible rather than permanently active.

evidence.summary: 3 of 4 Global Administrators have no strong auth method registered.

findings.title: Azure OpenAI deployment reachable over public network
findings.description: The Azure OpenAI account 'contoso-openai' has publicNetworkAccess=Enabled with no IP restrictions, exposing the inference endpoint and any deployed models to the internet (key-based auth only).
findings.attack_vector: If an API key leaks (e.g. in client code), the endpoint is directly callable from anywhere.
findings.risk: Model abuse, data exfiltration via prompts, and unbudgeted spend.
findings.recommendation: Set publicNetworkAccess=Disabled and use a private endpoint, or restrict to known IP ranges. Prefer Entra ID (managed identity) auth over API keys and rotate keys.

evidence.summary: publicNetworkAccess = Enabled; networkAcls default action = Allow.

defender_for_cloud: Cognitive Services accounts should restrict network access

findings.title: Key Vault has no diagnostic logging to a Log Analytics workspace
findings.description: Key Vault 'kv-web-prod' (the vault on the Critical attack path) has no diagnostic setting sending AuditEvent logs anywhere, so secret-read activity is invisible.
findings.attack_vector: An attacker reading secrets through the managed identity leaves no audit trail.
findings.risk: The most dangerous step in the Critical chain is undetectable — exploitable AND invisible.
findings.recommendation: Add a diagnostic setting on the vault sending AuditEvent (and AllMetrics) to a Log Analytics workspace, and alert on anomalous secret reads.

evidence.summary: No diagnostic settings configured on kv-web-prod.

findings.title: Web app served over TLS 1.0 with no Web Application Firewall
findings.description: The public portal accepts TLS 1.0/1.1 and is not fronted by Azure Front Door or Application Gateway WAF.
findings.attack_vector: Downgrade attacks and direct exploitation of the origin without a WAF inspection layer.
findings.risk: Weak transport security and no edge protection for the most-exposed app.
findings.recommendation: Set minimum TLS to 1.2+, and place the app behind Front Door or App Gateway with WAF in Prevention mode.

findings.title: No resource locks on production resource groups
findings.description: Production resource groups have no CanNotDelete or ReadOnly locks, so a compromised or mistaken Contributor can delete production resources.
findings.attack_vector: Destructive action (resource deletion) by any Contributor.
findings.risk: Availability impact; not a confidentiality issue on its own.
findings.recommendation: Apply CanNotDelete locks to production resource groups and critical resources.

evidence.summary: No management locks found on rg-web-prod.
